incidents-bot: 🚨 Incident detected: spike in routing errors between hosted and dedicated capacity tiers (spillback + tenant routing anomalies) — alert id=IR-2026-0315-42

Miguel (oncall): seeing 5xx rate jump for a subset of tenants, routing path shows Hosted -> Dedicated -> Hosted (spillback loop). pages ******* to SRE.

Lee (sre): acked. oncall moving to incident channel. quick check: are we seeing model-variant mismatches triggering fallback? logs show repeated 'variant-compat-fail' + policy fallback.

sarah (eng-runtime): adding context — we rolled a routing policy change ~10m ago that relaxed capacity-tier isolation for burstable requests (policy id: rt-policy-2026-03-relax). suspect that it's enabling hosted requests to be sent to dedicated pools, then fallback back to hosted when dedicated rejects due to tenant isolation, causing a loop.

Miguel (oncall): timeline: start 1872345600, policy rollout at 1872345605, errors spike at 1872345630. Impact: increased latency and ~30% failed request rate for affected tenants (IDs redacted), customer-facing errors for two midmarket customers.

Tim (support): getting tickets from two customers complaining about degraded responses and unexpected model outputs (timing out then sending older model variant). they want ETA.

Anya (product): flagging high-impact customers. we need immediate mitigation, then a successful rollback if necessary.

Lee (sre): mitigation plan: (1) pause routing policy rollout (flip to previous config), (2) enforce strict capacity-tier binding for the next 30m, (3) kill cross-tier fallback path, (4) throttle retries. Is everyone good with that order?

sarah (eng-runtime): agree. exact commands:
```bash
# rollback routing policy
redwoodctl routing policy rollback --id rt-policy-2026-03-relax --to-version v3
# lock capacity-tier to strict for hosted/dedicated
redwoodctl capacity-tier set --pool hosted --strict-tenant-binding true
redwoodctl capacity-tier set --pool dedicated --strict-tenant-binding true
# temporarily disable cross-tier fallback
redwoodctl routing feature-toggle set cross_tier_fallback false --scope global
```

Miguel (oncall): executing rollback now. I will run commands and post logs.

deploy-bot: @Miguel (oncall) initiated routing policy rollback rt-policy-2026-03-relax -> v3 at 1872345702.

Miguel (oncall): rollback command returned 0. monitoring metrics.

Lee (sre): I pushed strict-tenant-binding true to both pools at 1872345720. Also disabled cross-tier fallback at 1872345730.

incidents-bot: metric alert cleared for routing error rate at 1872345799. 5xxs falling back toward baseline.

Tim (support): told both customers we have mitigations in place and are monitoring, ETA preliminary 30m for stability.

Anya (product): please also gather affected request samples and model variant traces for postmortem. need to know if requests hit an unexpected model variant after the loop.

sarah (eng-runtime): collecting traces. found examples where gateway routed to dedicated pool running model: open-model-v2-qt, which rejected due to tenant ACL mismatch, then gateway retried to hosted but selected older variant open-model-v1, so customers saw inconsistent model outputs. saving logs to /var/logs/incidents/1872345678/trace.log

Lee (sre): immediate customer impact: increased error rates and stale/older-model responses for a subset of requests during the 3–8 minute window. Root cause hypothesis: policy relaxation + missing ACL validation in the early routing decision allowed requests to enter dedicated pools where tenant mismatch triggered fallback, which then selected a different model variant.

Miguel (oncall): current status: stabilized. blockers: need a fast guard in the routing layer to validate tenant-model compatibility before sending to another tier.

sarah (eng-runtime): action items created:
- ENG-RUNTIME-442: add pre-routing tenant-model compatibility check (high)
- ENG-PLATFORM-551: policy rollout safer defaults (auto-rollback if error x% within y mins)
- SRE-203: post-incident validation runbook update (include steps to lock tiers and disable cross-tier fallback)

Anya (product): create customer comms draft and share with GTM. Tim will coordinate follow ups.

Tim (support): will follow up with ticket updates in 15m.

Lee (sre): proposing postmortem meeting 1h from now. owners for mitigation and followups: Miguel (oncall), sarah (eng-runtime), Lee (sre), Anya (product), Tim (support).

Miguel (oncall): thanks all. leaving incident channel open until postmortem. :white_check_mark:

incidents-bot: Incident IR-2026-0315-42 status=mitigated, severity=high, duration=7m22s, paged: 2 oncall(s), affected-customers: 2 (midmarket).
